name: Reaper Farm vault missing access control on deposit-for

classification.summary: The Reaper vault exposed a deposit path that took the source address as a parameter with no check that it was the caller, so anyone could pull tokens from every wallet that had approved the vault.

loss.notes: Migrated from legacy lossUsd/lossOther. The legacy corpus did not consistently distinguish gross from net loss or record valuation provenance.

limitations: Target identity and code history came from the v1 snapshot row originally at protocols/reaper-farm.json; no semantic revalidation was inherited.
The executing code artifact and its code hash have not been established in structured evidence.
One or more target block, transaction, ordering, or creator anchors remain unresolved.

sources.note: onchain review on Fantom over a public RPC: the PoC carries no transaction hash, so the exploit tx was recovered by querying eth_getLogs on the vault 0xcdA5deA176F2dF95082f4daDb96255Bdb2bc7C7D across the PoC's fork block window (44045897-44045905), which yields 0xc929f3b9...c9d5 at block 44045900 with ten logs. Creation resolved by binary search over eth_getCode to block 41839240, 2022-07-02T12:48:36Z, creator 0x6539519e69343535a2af6583d9bae3ad74c6a293, not the attack-tx sender 0x5636e55e4a72299a0f194c001841e2ce75bb527a; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, 30.7 days old. Loss ~1.7M US$ across multiple ERC-20s per the DeFiHackLabs 2022 index entry for this PoC.
